# Perform Harvey test for multiplicative heteroscedasticity

<small>Source: [`man/performHarveyTest.Rd`](https://github.com/DiogoRibeiro7/heteroTests/blob/main/man/performHarveyTest.Rd) · Help: `?performHarveyTest`</small>

Harvey's (1976) Lagrange multiplier test, which regresses `log(residuals^2)` on a set of variance regressors.

## Usage

```r
performHarveyTest(model, data = NULL, auxiliary = c("regressors", "fitted"),
                  studentize = FALSE)
```

## Arguments

`model`
:   an object of class `lm`.

`data`
:   optional data frame the model was fitted to. When `NULL`, the default, the model frame of `model` is used. The statistic is computed from the residuals, fitted values and model matrix of `model`, so `data` does not change the result; it is accepted so that every test takes `(model, data, ...)`. Before 0.15.0 the second argument was `auxiliary` and the third `studentize`: a string passed second by position, and a logical value after it, are still read as those two, with a warning that shows the new call; that form stops working in 1.0.0.

`auxiliary`
:   character scalar choosing the variance regressors. `"regressors"` (the default) uses the model's own explanatory variables, the specification in Harvey (1976). `"fitted"` uses the fitted values and their square, which was the behaviour of releases before 0.7.0.

`studentize`
:   logical; if `FALSE` (the default) the chi-square statistic \(\mathrm{ESS} / (\pi^2 / 2)\) is reported, otherwise the auxiliary regression F statistic.

## Value

An object of class `htest` containing the test statistic, its degrees of freedom and the p-value.

## Details

Harvey (1976) models the error variance as \(\sigma_i^2 = \exp(z_i^\top \gamma)\) and tests \(\gamma = 0\) through the auxiliary regression of \(\log \hat{e}_i^2\) on \(z_i\). Under the null the auxiliary error behaves like a centred \(\log \chi^2_1\) variate with variance \(\pi^2 / 2 \approx 4.9348\), so the classical statistic is \(\mathrm{ESS} / (\pi^2 / 2)\), asymptotically chi-square with \(q\) degrees of freedom.

Setting `studentize = TRUE` replaces the fixed constant \(\pi^2 / 2\) with the auxiliary residual mean square and refers the overall F statistic to an F distribution. The two forms are asymptotically equivalent under normal errors; the studentized form is more reliable when normality is doubtful, because \(\pi^2 / 2\) is the null variance of \(\log \hat{e}^2\) only for Gaussian errors.

Degrees of freedom are taken from the realised rank of the auxiliary design, so a rank-deficient variance model is not credited with degrees of freedom for aliased columns.

## Validation

The default statistic reproduces an independent reconstruction of Harvey (1976) to within `1e-8`; see `tests/testthat/test-pass-a-reference.R`. Simulated size and power are recorded in `inst/validation/pass-a-size-power.csv`.

## References

Harvey, A. C. (1976). Estimating regression models with multiplicative heteroscedasticity. *Econometrica*, 44(3), 461–465. [doi:10.2307/1913974](https://doi.org/10.2307/1913974)

Greene, W. H. (2018). *Econometric Analysis* (8th ed.). Pearson. Section 9.5 derives the \(\mathrm{ESS} / 4.9348\) form of the statistic.

## Examples

```r
 data(mtcars)
 m <- lm(mpg ~ wt + qsec, data = mtcars)
 performHarveyTest(m)

 # Studentized variant, which does not assume normal errors
 performHarveyTest(m, studentize = TRUE)

 # Variance driven by the conditional mean rather than by the regressors
 performHarveyTest(m, auxiliary = "fitted")
```
